sources.author: Kuikanmäki, Jari, and Matti Virtanen
sources.title: Did the Wuhan Virus Institute Trigger the Coronavirus Pandemic? – More Evidence for the Laboratory Theory
sources.summary: Author’s archived AlfaTV piece arguing accumulating evidence that WIV may have triggered the pandemic—Finnish-language lab-theory roundup.
sources.book_role: Author’s own contemporary synthesis as NIH admissions and new relatives emerge—Chapter 17’s enigma frame.

sources.title: Understanding the Risk of Bat Coronavirus Emergence (including the Year-5 Interim RPPR)
sources.summary: NIH FOIA release of EcoHealth bat-coronavirus emergence materials including the late Year-5 interim RPPR describing WIV experiments.
sources.book_role: Document dump that forced NIH’s public reckoning with funded Wuhan virus work.

sources.author: Tabak, Lawrence
sources.title: Letter to Rep. Cathy McMorris Rodgers (House Committee on Energy and Commerce), regarding EcoHealth Alliance grant materials
sources.publication: National Institutes of Health, Department of Health and Human Services
sources.summary: NIH Principal Deputy Director Lawrence Tabak’s letter to Rep. McMorris Rodgers transmitting EcoHealth grant materials and acknowledging limited experiments that should have triggered further review.
sources.book_role: Official NIH admission letter that shifted the ‘we never funded risky Wuhan research’ line.

orgs: U.S. House Energy and Commerce Committee

sources.author: Eban, Katherine
sources.title: In Major Shift, NIH Admits Funding Risky Virus Research in Wuhan
sources.summary: Vanity Fair on NIH’s major shift admitting it funded risky virus research in Wuhan via EcoHealth—coverage of the Tabak letter fallout.
sources.book_role: Mainstream framing of the NIH admission as a turning point in the enigma.

sources.author: Mallapaty, Smriti
sources.title: Closest known relatives of virus behind COVID-19 found in Laos
sources.summary: Nature news on BANAL bat coronaviruses from Laos—closer relatives to SARS-CoV-2 than RaTG13 in key spike regions—complicating simple Wuhan-only stories.
sources.book_role: New natural-relative evidence that deepens rather than resolves the origin enigma.

sources.author: Demaneuf, Gilles
sources.title: Overview of Biological Laboratories in Wuhan and their roles in Coronavirus Research
sources.summary: Demaneuf overview mapping Wuhan’s biological laboratories and their coronavirus-research roles—beyond WIV alone.
sources.book_role: Widens the enigma: multiple Wuhan labs, not a single building.

sources.author: Pekar, Jonathan, et al.
sources.title: Timing the SARS-CoV-2 index case in Hubei province
sources.summary: Science paper timing the SARS-CoV-2 index case in Hubei—molecular-clock estimates of when the outbreak began relative to reported December cases.
sources.book_role: Chronological constraint on the enigma: when did human transmission start?

sources.author: Washburne, Alex
sources.title: Zoonotic Origin Evidence We Don't Have
sources.summary: Washburne Substack cataloging zoonotic-origin evidence that is still missing—intermediate hosts, early animal positives, market chain—versus what lab-leak critics demand.
sources.book_role: Negative-evidence checklist keeping the zoonosis claim incomplete.

sources.author: Zhan, Shing Hei, et al.
sources.title: SARS-CoV-2 is well adapted for humans. What does this mean for re-emergence?
sources.summary: Early bioRxiv preprint arguing SARS-CoV-2 appears well adapted to humans from the outset—flagged later in classified analyses for FCS/adaptation implications (chapter notes).
sources.book_role: Adaptation puzzle that resists a simple fresh-spillover story.

sources.author: Fauci, Anthony S.
sources.title: Research on Highly Pathogenic H5N1 Influenza Virus: The Way Forward
sources.summary: Fauci’s 2012 mBio commentary defending a path forward for highly pathogenic H5N1 research amid gain-of-function controversy.
sources.book_role: Fauci’s own prior GoF philosophy—context for later Wuhan-funding denials.

sources.author: Klotz, Lynn
sources.title: Human error in high-biocontainment labs: a likely pandemic threat
sources.summary: Pre-COVID Bulletin warning that human error in high-biocontainment labs is a likely pandemic threat—lab-accident risk as mainstream biosafety concern.
sources.book_role: 2019 baseline: lab accidents were predicted pandemic pathways before COVID.

sources.title: Competitive Consultation on Central Air Conditioning Renovation Project of the Wuhan Institute of Virology
sources.publication: China Government Procurement Network, Chinese Academy of Sciences
sources.summary: Archived Sept 2019 procurement notice for WIV central air-conditioning renovation—cited in debates over pre-outbreak lab infrastructure problems. Thin archive capture.
sources.book_role: Biosafety-infrastructure clue timed just before the outbreak window.

sources.author: Dilanian, Ken, et al.
sources.title: Report says cellphone data suggests October shutdown at Wuhan lab, but experts are skeptical
sources.summary: NBC/Yahoo report on a disputed claim that cellphone data showed an October 2019 Wuhan-lab shutdown—experts skeptical.
sources.book_role: Contested early-signal claim in the timeline enigma—possible precursor event vs noise.

sources.author: Allen, Nick
sources.title: US and UK intelligence agencies 'examining report on mobile phone data at Wuhan laboratory'
sources.summary: Archived Telegraph report that U.S. and UK intelligence were examining the mobile-phone data claims about the Wuhan laboratory.
sources.book_role: Shows intel interest in the same contested October-activity signal.

sources.author: Ai, Hongxia
sources.title: Dedicated airport port-of-entry for the Military World Games opened for testing
sources.summary: Xinhua (archived) on opening a dedicated airport port-of-entry for the Wuhan Military World Games testing—pre-outbreak mass international military gathering in Wuhan.
sources.book_role: Timeline context: major military sports event in Wuhan weeks before recognized outbreak.

sources.author: Quay, Steven Carl
sources.title: Where Did the 2019 Coronavirus Pandemic Begin and How Did it Spread? The People's Liberation Army Hospital in Wuhan China and Line 2 of the Wuhan Metro System Are Compelling Answers
sources.summary: Quay Zenodo preprint arguing PLA hospital and Wuhan Metro Line 2 as compelling early-spread nodes—alternative geography of the outbreak’s start.
sources.book_role: Alternative spatial hypothesis inside the enigma: military hospital and metro, not only the market.
